title: Fuel invariance of the canonical decision tree continuation
statement: The canonical decision tree of a DNF formula $f$ under a restriction $\rho$ is built by a fuel-limited recursion; write $G_k(f,\rho)$ for the decision tree it returns when run with fuel budget $k \in \bbn$ starting from $\rho$, so that the canonical decision tree of $f$ under $\rho$ is $G_{m(\rho)+1}(f,\rho)$, where $m(\rho)$ denotes the number of free variables of $\rho$. Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables, let $t$ be a term with $t \in f$, and let $\rho_{\mathrm{orig}}$ and $\rho'$ be restrictions with $m(\rho_{\mathrm{orig}}) \ge m(\rho') + 1$. Then the tree that returns the constant-true leaf if $t$ is fixed by $\rho'$ and returns $G_{m(\rho_{\mathrm{orig}})}(f,\rho')$ otherwise is equal to the canonical decision tree of $f$ under $\rho'$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
t is a term belonging to f
m(rho_orig) >= m(rho') + 1 (fuel bound on numbers of free variables)
caveat: The lemma is a fuel-bookkeeping identity for the recursion that defines the canonical decision tree: the fuel budget and the fuel-limited helper are implementation scaffolding without a clean standalone textbook meaning, so the faithful rendering necessarily exposes the fuel parameter rather than a purely mathematical object.
replaced:
For $t \in f$ and a restriction $\rho'$ with $\rho_{\mathrm{orig}}.\mathrm{numFree} \ge \rho'.\mathrm{numFree} + 1$,
the standard continuation $\bigl(\text{if } t \text{ fixed by } \rho' \text{ then } \mathrm{leaf}\ \mathrm{true}\ \text{else}\ \mathrm{canonicalDTree.go}\,f\,\rho_{\mathrm{orig}}.\mathrm{numFree}\,\rho'\bigr)$
equals $\mathrm{canonicalDTree}\,f\,\rho'$.
